title: Redwood Private VPC Security Architecture Deep Dive with Avalon Trust
customer_attendees: Rafael Ortiz - Head of Cloud Engineering
meeting_header: Date: 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC; Duration: 62 minutes; Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE), Marco Liu (Redwood SE), Diane Cole (CISO, Avalon), Rafael Ortiz (Head of Cloud Eng), Maya Patel (Security Architect)
summary: Deep dive on private/VPC deployment security architecture: network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, audit logs, KMS/ encryption options, SSO/RBAC mapping, and SOC2/ISO artifacts. Agreed next steps around sending SOC2/ISO docs, VPC wiring diagram, and scheduling on-site network review and pilot benchmark.
topics: SOC2/ISO evidence and pen test policy
Data residency and network egress policies
transcript:
[00:00] Priya: hi everyone thanks for joining, im priya nair from redwood AE. we have marco se on the line for the architecture deep dive.
[00:07] Marco: hey team, great to meet you all, i'll walk through the vpc wiring and how we do isolation, ingress/egress and key mgmt.
[00:15] Diane: thanks, main thing for us is we need strict network isolation and control of any egress to third party internet, also SOC2 evidence and KMS options.
[00:25] Rafael: yes and we have a corporate firewall policy — default deny, only approved outbound egress via our proxy. we need to know if redwood private respects that model and how control plane connectivity works.
[00:38] Marco: totally. quick agenda: control plane vs data plane, customer-managed VPC wiring, ingress patterns (private endpoints, load balancer), egress policies (nat gateway or VPC endpoints), firewalling and IDS, ksm — sorry kms integration, audit logs and SIEM forwarding, sso/rbac mapping, and compliance artifacts.
[00:55] Maya: quick q, does redwood control plane ever see plaintext PII or is everything end-to-end encrypted?
[01:06] Marco: good q. in the private deployment we offer a customer-controlled data plane inside your VPC; the control plane can be hosted in our managed region or delivered as a private-control-plane option. data in transit to compute is TLS 1.2/1.3; at rest encryption is AES-256. if you enable BYOK, the customer-managed key material never leaves your KMS. there is an option for HSM-backed keys for higher assurance.
[01:40] Diane: when you say control plane hosted by redwood, what network path is used? we cannot allow arbitrary inbound connections from public internet into our VPC.
[01:51] Priya: right — for the hosted-control-plane option we use a private endpoint that you provision (AWS PrivateLink or Azure Private Endpoint). this creates an interface endpoint inside your VPC and all control traffic is over that private link. if you choose the private-control-plane deployment we either install the control plane into your account or provide an on-prem package; in both cases no public ingress is required.
[02:14] Rafael: ok, so for PrivateLink we still need to manage security groups on the endpoint, are there recommended SG rules?
[02:22] Marco: yes recommended pattern: interface endpoint SG is very tight — allow only the management CIDRs from your admin subnets and the Redwood worker subnets if using cross-account. we support mTLS for control plane auth if you want mutual TLS on top.
[02:34] Diane: what about egress — we have a policy to only allow outbound to specific IP ranges for vendor apis and block everything else. how does redwood handle model updates, container images etc?
[02:46] Marco: for model onboarding and image pulls we provide two options: 1) the images can be pushed to your private registry (ECR/ACR) and your workers pull from there via private peering, or 2) we can mirror artifacts into your VPC via an agreed artifact mirror. if you use the mirror approach we provide pre-signed artifacts over the private link. so no need for public internet egress.
[03:10] Rafael: good. and logs — we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM (splunk) and retain for 7 years for some regs.
[03:18] Priya: we can stream audit/log events to your Kinesis/CloudWatch/Log Analytics or directly to syslog/Splunk via a forwarder. we also retain an immutable audit trail in the control plane; we can configure retention windows and export snapshots. note that some control-plane telemetry requires metadata exchange — we will document which events are present.
[03:36] Maya: are audit logs tamper-evident and signed? we have to prove chain of custody for certain investigations.
[03:44] Marco: the logs are integrity-protected — we support signing of log bundles and can create hash chains. For highest assurance you can forward logs to your own WORM storage or to an HSM-backed logging system.
[03:56] Diane: about RBAC and SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and have strict role mappings. can we map our Okta groups to redwood roles?
[04:05] Priya: yes, we integrate with SAML/OIDC. mapping is flexible — we support group-to-role mapping and SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. Marco, anything on just-in-time role sync?
[04:14] Marco: we do JIT for auth tokens and periodic sync for groups; for tight enterprises we recommend SCIM so you have full control. we also support session duration controls and forced re-auth.
[04:24] Rafael: one more on keys — if we use AWS KMS with BYOK, do you store any copy of the DEKs?
[04:31] Marco: no, in BYOK mode the data encryption keys are wrapped by your CMK in your KMS; Redwood never holds the unwrapped DEK. we keep only encrypted blobs. if you want HSM we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or on-prem HSM via PKCS#11.
[04:50] Maya: nice. does rotation require downtime?
[04:53] Marco: rotation is seamless — we rewrap existing DEKs with the new CMK version in a background job and rotate for new writes. older logs remain decryptable via the KMS key history.
[05:02] Diane: penetration tests and vulnerability management — we run internal pentests but we need vendor attestation and periodic scans of deployed infra.
[05:11] Priya: Redwood provides weekly vulnerability scans for our managed images and quarterly pen test reports for the platform; for private deployments we can run agreed scans in your environment or provide our SOC2 penetration summary and remediation timelines.
[05:27] Rafael: what about network IDS/IPS and egress monitoring? do you offer inline inspection or do we need to provide that?
[05:33] Marco: we recommend putting workers in private subnets behind your IDS/IPS. we can optionally integrate with a sidecar that emits network telemetry to your IDS. for inline DPI we typically recommend a customer-managed appliance — Redwood focuses on telemetry and hooks for integration, not being the inline network firewall.
[05:49] Maya: firewall rules for model serving ports — what ports are needed?
[05:53] Marco: serving typically listens on 443 for TLS. internal KV cache and worker comms use ephemeral high ports; we'll provide a port matrix. best practice is default deny and allow only the expected CIDRs.
[06:03] Diane: do you support egress proxies that require authentication? our egress goes through an authenticated proxy.
[06:09] Marco: yes we support proxied egress with token-based auth for outbound. we'll need proxy creds or a forwarder hosted in the VPC. we also support static egress IPs for allowlisting — that's available in the Dedicated/Private deployments.
[06:22] Rafael: static egress IPs are important for our payment processors. is that per-customer?
[06:28] Priya: yes, we can allocate static egress NAT IPs for your deployment, and document them for your processors. if you host on-prem we can NAT via your appliance.
[06:36] Maya: questions on control-plane event visibility — if the control plane is hosted by redwood, can we get full audit of admin actions?
[06:43] Marco: yes control-plane audit logs include admin actions, config changes, and role grants. we can push those to your SIEM. when control plane is private-in-account you have even more direct visibility.
[06:56] Diane: data residency — all compute and storage must remain in our chosen region (us-east-2). is that supported?
[07:03] Priya: yes region pinning is supported; for private deployments we run all resources in your region. for hosted control plane we ensure metadata routing stays regional and we offer region-specific control planes for enterprise.
[07:15] Rafael: about certificate management for mutual TLS, can we provide our own CA?
[07:21] Marco: you can bring your own CA for mTLS certs. Redwood supports uploading certificate bundles and we can integrate with your internal PKI via SCEP or ACME depending on setup.
[07:33] Diane: what's the SLA for forensic log export requests? we might need historical logs for investigations.
[07:39] Priya: we have an SLA for evidence requests; usually we can export and sign log bundles within 48 hours for standard requests, urgent requests can be accelerated. we'll include this in the security deck.
[07:49] Rafael: compliance docs — can you share SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs and a redacted pen test report?
[07:55] Priya: absolutely, i'll include links to our SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 certificate, and our penetration test summary.
[08:02] Maya: do you have a formal change mgmt / release schedule that we can align maintenance windows with?
[08:09] Marco: yes we have a change mgmt calendar; for private deployments we offer maintenance windows you control, and we provide advance notices and post-mortems.
[08:20] Diane: network ACLs vs security groups — what's recommended?
[08:24] Marco: security groups for instance-level controls and NACLs for subnet-level defense in depth. both are supported; we recommend security groups for allow rules and NACLs for an additional stateless check.
[08:36] Rafael: curious about patching of worker nodes — who is responsible?
[08:40] Priya: in private deployments customers can choose to manage worker OS patching or opt into Redwood-managed worker images where we handle patching and images are validated. we document CVE fixes and EOL timelines.
[08:54] Maya: do you support FIPS endpoints for cryptography?
[08:58] Marco: yes FIPS-compliant crypto modules are available for customers that need it. we'll provide documentation on FIPS modes and supported libraries.
[09:07] Diane: how are credentials for service accounts handled?
[09:10] Marco: service accounts use short-lived credentials with automatic rotation. we support workload identity federation, so you can avoid long-lived IAM keys.
[09:20] Rafael: can you talk about network segmentation inside the VPC for multi-tenant customers? we want heavy segmentation and tagging.
[09:27] Marco: in private deployments each customer gets tenant-dedicated subnets and security boundary. worker pools can be segmented by workload type and you can enforce tag-based RBAC for resources. we also support firewall policies per-tenant.
[09:42] Maya: any gotchas for direct connect / expressroute?
[09:45] Priya: you can use DX/ER to route traffic without traversing public internet; ensure routing policies and BGP are configured to only advertise required prefixes. we can help with route filters and prefix planning.
[09:59] Diane: audit question — are admin activity logs accessible for the last 12 months by default?
[10:04] Marco: by default we retain 90 days in the control plane UI; longer retention (12 months, 7 years) can be configured and exported to your storage. there might be additional cost for long-term retention.
[10:17] Rafael: how do you handle secrets in config (api keys for downstream integrations)?
[10:22] Marco: secrets are stored encrypted using the CMK; we provide a secrets store interface and audit for access. we never log plaintext secrets.
[10:30] Maya: can we run a network benchmark / proof-of-concept? want to validate latency and egress patterns.
[10:36] Priya: yes we typically do a 2-week pilot with dedicated capacity on your VPC. we'll run perf benchmarks and a security runbook.
[10:45] Diane: ok let's talk deliverables and next steps.
[10:48] Priya: next steps: i'll share SOC2/ISO certs and security deck; marco will send the recommended VPC wiring diagram and port matrix; raf will get a proposal for static egress IPs and pilot pricing; schedule a follow-up on-site network review.
[10:59] Rafael: sounds good. can we also have a contact for incident response?
[11:03] Priya: yes our security ops on-call contact is included in the security pack.
[11:09] Marco: i'll also include example terraform modules for deploying private endpoints and the worker subnet layout.
[11:16] Diane: one more question — do you allow external audit teams to run tests in our environment?
[11:21] Marco: yes with coordination — we have an attestation process and can whitelist scanners and testers. we'll work with your vendor for timing and scope.
[11:33] Priya: thanks everyone. we'll recap in an email with artifacts.
[11:38] Diane: thank you, very thorough.
[11:40] Rafael: appreciate it.
[11:42] Maya: thanks.
[11:44] Priya: end.
